name: ScriptaHub – Edit book
description: Generate or revise the current HTML book, using an uploaded manuscript as the source when present, then validate and publish.
defaultObjective: Reserve submitted new-edition tasks exclusively. Process each book edition as one task containing all approved requests selected at submission; later approvals wait for another edition. Record each confirmed publication result in ScriptaHub.

tasks.name: Reserve batch and select first request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Run preflight and batch-start with {"taskType":"edit"} from the flow root once. The helper resumes queued/active reservations or replaces a service-confirmed closed/exhausted batch. This selector is the parent entry point.

Use batch-next to obtain one reserved task and its durable claimedPath/handoffPath. Return those paths, taskDirectory and executionId. Route publicationPending=true to batch-to-publication for reconciliation of the same execution; route a running processing item to batch-to-item. Route task=null to batch-to-result. For a pre-claim prerequisite failure, close the batch when safe and report the actual error through batch-to-result. Keep an unresolved active/publication execution bound to this lot until reconciled.

tasks.name: Select next reserved request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Continue the saved batch after the preceding request is service-confirmed terminal. Call only batch-next for selection and keep later arrivals for the next parent execution. Refresh preflight when its validity expires.

Use batch-next to obtain one reserved task and its durable claimedPath/handoffPath. Return those paths, taskDirectory and executionId. Route publicationPending=true to next-to-publication for reconciliation of the same execution; route a running processing item to next-to-item. Route task=null to next-to-result. For a pre-claim prerequisite failure, close the batch when safe and report the actual error through next-to-result. Keep an unresolved active/publication execution bound to this lot until reconciled.

tasks.name: Prepare the new edition
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the exact claimed task and processingSettings supplied by the selector. Do not claim again or generate a runId. Check the task status. Preserve the complete requests array (including each request’s approved annotations, values, language, files and original baseRevision), the edition baseRevision and configured repositories under <taskDirectory>/run-state/edit.json. On a verified running task take claim-to-edit; otherwise take claim-to-result with the actual reason. Never access private ScriptaHub storage or credentials.

tasks.name: Apply approved changes
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the claimed edition task and every entry in task.requests. Produce one new edition combining the complete snapshotted request set. Apply only approved annotations and the values supplied for those requests; rejected annotations are absent and must not be fetched or reconstructed. Keep request IDs paired with annotation IDs, which can repeat across requests. Preserve every request’s language and document indexes. Use document-read with the global file indexes supplied by ScriptaHub. Do not fetch newly approved requests or select additional changes. If accepted changes contradict one another or cannot be applied safely to the existing edition, fail this task with precise conflicting passages rather than silently skipping either change. Produce one jointly edited edition and one publication package. Locate its existing book in the configured repositories; do not choose a different book or create a new one. Read the actual branch and pin its remote commit as the publication baseline. Download the existing metadata and resources into this task's working directory without credentials. Verify each annotation's edition, exact quote and prefix/suffix in the corresponding full HTML edition; Interpret offsets against the reader's textContent. Never apply ambiguous or stale annotations to another passage. Apply every approved annotation and no rejected or unrelated changes. Produce a new edition, retaining previous edition files unchanged. Update only this book's manifest/edition history or book.json and its catalogue entry. Preserve the book ID and location. Record each annotation’s implemented change and paths, identified by its request ID plus annotation ID. If the existing book, source passage, or required resources cannot be verified, record an actionable error and take edit-to-submit. Otherwise take edit-to-validation.

Before changing anything, retain an immutable local copy of the original HTML and every referenced resource, with working relative paths and SHA-256 hashes. Record the affected editions in an editions array in <taskDirectory>/run-state/edit.json, with language, baselineHtml, candidateHtml and changesPath for each. Keep a separate immutable baseline and change file for each affected edition. Build each changesPath file as an array of {annotationId,before,after,prefix,suffix} for approved textual replacements only. In this report, annotationId is the request ID followed by a colon and the original annotation ID; retain their original pair in edit.json. before must be the exact approved quote; after is the actual authorized replacement. Use [] for presentation-only changes with unchanged wording. Do not list unrelated changes or let this file authorize additional edits. Do not run whole-book PDF correction or change language editions not referenced by approved requests. Preserve existing images and resources.

An explicit new-edition request can contain general revision instructions in request.values.feedback without annotations. Apply only those authorized instructions and preserve attribution, existing book identity and edition history. Include the full resulting HTML book and preserve supplied manuscript resources according to the source profile. For purely presentation changes, keep wording unchanged and the textual replacement report empty. Record any specifically authorized textual replacements against the exact baseline passages in the regression evidence; do not invent annotation approvals.

tasks.name: Check the new edition is ready to publish
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Validate the prepared edition only for regressions caused by the approved suggestions. Read every affected edition from the editions array in <taskDirectory>/run-state/edit.json. Validate each separately using its baselineHtml, candidateHtml and changesPath; never validate only the first request or language. Use the native validate-book command through scriptahub-tasks exec: compare-edition BASELINE_HTML --candidate CANDIDATE_HTML --changes CHANGES_PATH --job-dir <taskDirectory>/validation/edit-layout-LANGUAGE. Substitute the actual paths and edition language; use a distinct native job directory for each edition. Paths are relative to this run. The deployed ScriptaHub reader stylesheet is provided by the runtime. The checker compares standalone and imported-reader presentation at desktop and mobile widths, confirms text is unchanged outside approved replacements, preserves image bytes and counts, and reports newly introduced overlaps, clipping, hidden content, overflow and broken resources. Compare read-only against the pinned baseline edition. Apply the revised-edition acceptance profile to the affected languages. Existing findings are reported as warnings; only new or worsened regressions block publication.

Keep this acceptance step read-only. Any new regression prohibits approval; retain the exact native findings for the request result. Record the actual native report and error counts; never fabricate a successful audit. Confirm approved annotations were addressed, old edition resources and other books remain unchanged, and catalogue references resolve. On success prepare the exact publication inventory and validation JSON required by scriptahub_task_package_prepare: executionId, runId, bookId, publicationPermitted:true, audit.scope edition_layout_regression, audit.autoCorrect:false, audit.status passed or passed_with_warnings, audit.errorFindings:0. Include every edition’s baseline/candidate hashes and native report path. Approve the package only when all these native reports pass; combine their actual error totals and preserve passed_with_warnings if any report has warnings. A failed or missing report blocks the entire edition, without publishing a partial selection of requests. Include catalogue and book metadata and all referenced resources with byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes; preserve the remote baseline. On failure retain the findings and do not write an approving inventory. Take validation-to-submit.

tasks.name: Publish the new edition
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Finalize this edition request using taskDirectory/run-state/edit.json and the actual service status. For a terminal execution, report its saved result. For publicationPending=true or a lost publication reply, call retry-publication for the same registered package. Preserve an unresolved result and stop traversal until reconciled.

For a confirmed stop before publication, acknowledge through finish state=cancelled. For a confirmed processing/validation failure before publication, call finish state=failed with the real error. Otherwise publish the exact independently approved package using its recorded catalogue, branch, inventory and validation paths. A service-confirmed completed state and receipt establish publication.

Save the response and concise evidence paths. After confirmed terminal state, take result-to-next to select-next-task. Points accounting and reward settlement remain with ScriptaHub/UserPersisto.

tasks.name: Summarize publication results
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the durable batch through scriptahub-tasks batch-status with {}; this returns the original snapshot without reserving anything, never new arrivals. Report actual completed, failed, cancelled and unprocessed counts and the relative artifact directories. If the batch is not closed and no task remains active, use batch-close to release unstarted reservations. Never overwrite an uncertain publication or claim more work. Report any preflight or service failure precisely. This is the end of the batch; do not loop or start another flow.
